title: AI-empowered next-generation multiscale climate modelling for mitigation and adaptation
testbed_rationale: Perspective article outlining a roadmap for AI-empowered multiscale Earth system modelling; does not create, evaluate, or release any dataset.
pain_points: Legacy languages (Fortran, C) hinder running on modern accelerator hardware (GPUs/TPUs) and prevent seamless online ML coupling
Out-of-distribution generalization failure (extrapolation beyond training regime)
Numerical instabilities when ML parameterizations are coupled online with host climate models
Staggering computational cost of century-scale simulations at kilometre resolution
Sparse, noisy, and indirect observational data making ML parameter inference challenging
Lack of uncertainty quantification in parameter tuning and ML emulators
Processes that do not improve purely with higher spatial resolution (e.g., biological systems, cryosphere, land processes)
extraction_notes: Perspective paper outlining four pillars for future climate modelling: accelerated computing/differentiable programming, hybrid physics-ML ESMs, model-data fusion with Earth observations, and modernized science infrastructures.
